authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: Don't dilute Pirate density for generic Grixis value creatures.
Don't trim blocker removal/protection just to add more Pirates.
Don't add one-shot effects unless they convert a key combat into theft or a kill.

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Blockers or fog effects stop the third Pirate from connecting, so no steal.
mitigations: Cyclonic Rift on a key turn

blueprint_failure_modes.description: A board wipe removes the Pirate density the condition needs.
Beckett removed repeatedly: the theft engine and anthem are gone.

value.interaction: Blocker removal and one-sided sweepers matter more than counters; keep ~8-11 interaction pieces.
value.mana: Four-mana commander; Treasure makers and rocks; 33 lands.
value.protection: Greaves plus free protection (Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat); the anthem dies with Beckett.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Beckett is both the anthem and the theft engine; the deck's evasion, token and Pirate-density choices exist to meet his three-Pirate condition.
accepted_role.honest_note: The three-different-Pirates-to-the-same-player condition is genuinely hard to meet through blockers, and the payoff is one steal per end step (two with Roaming Throne). Without evasion the deck is ordinary tribal aggro.

reviews.question: Can the deck rebuild after repeated removal across multiple permanent types?
